teaser.text: Parker Hannifin is a maker of the parts and systems hidden inside industrial machines, aircraft and refrigeration equipment. To understand its business, follow a dollar from the component Parker engineers and makes, through the customer and distributor, to the replacement sale that may come later.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Parker, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case falls to $4,850M in 2027 and $4,650M in 2028 before recovering to $4,900M. It assumes delayed industrial replenishment, slower aerospace shipments and acquisition costs before savings. The bull case reaches $6,000M in 2027 and $6,750M in 2028, then $7,540M, requiring broad recovery and faster savings. These outcomes reflect the gap between the 20.5% five-year margin average and the latest result.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Parker really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation creates a further adjustment. Parker recognized $179 million of stock-based compensation in fiscal 2026. Because that expense does not immediately consume cash, it is added back in operating cash flow. But employees receive shares or share-linked awards, which can dilute existing owners. Deducting it produces an analytical “real free cash flow” of $3,726 million.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Parker today?

paragraphs.text: At **$956.32 a share on October 15, 2026**, Parker trades at **33.6 times** its last twelve months’ earnings. It trades at **24.3 times** expected earnings for the next twelve months. The first is trailing P/E; the second is forward P/E. A $100 share costing 33 times earnings at $3 of profit can cost 24 times when expected profit rises to $4.10. The price has not become cheaper; the expected earnings have become larger. That forecast must therefore be tested, especially because the first fiscal 2027 outlook excluded recent acquisitions.

Free cash flow is the money left after running the business and maintaining its equipment. Parker’s **3.2% free-cash-flow yield** says that each $100 of market value represents about $3.20 of annual cash generation, not that the investor receives $3.20. The dividend yield was only **0.8%**. Parker can use the rest for acquisitions, debt repayment or repurchases. Working capital also matters: a credit sale can produce accounting profit before the customer pays, while inventory consumes cash before it is sold.

dividend.title: Parker dividend: cash coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: Parker pays an annual dividend supported by strong free cash flow, with future increases depending on growth, debt and acquisition execution.
dividend.opening: Parker pays $8.00 per share annually, with the forecast showing $8.40 in 2027, $9.24 in 2028 and $10.16 in 2029. Parker's $3,905 million of fiscal 2026 free cash flow covers its dividend, while cash also funds buybacks, acquisitions and debt reduction.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Parker's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Parker pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends start from the current $8.00 annualized rate. The base case pays $8.40 per share in 2027, $9.24 in 2028 and $10.16 in 2029. That represents roughly 10% annual increases, close to the latest 11% raise. The bear case uses $8.20, $8.61 and $9.04 as debt and integration demands restrain increases. The bull case reaches $8.60, $10.12 and $11.96 because cash conversion remains strong. The 70-year increase record supports continued payments.

blocks.heading: Does Parker's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Cash conversion asks how much reported earnings become money generated by the business. After capital spending, Parker produced $3,905 million of free cash flow in fiscal 2026. That equaled 107% of net income, compared with approximately 95% in fiscal 2025. Cash generation therefore strengthened even though the prior year benefited from unusually favourable tax items.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to 5.5%–8.5% reported and organic sales growth for fiscal 2027. The adjusted EPS guide is $34.25–$35.25. Adjusted segment margin is guided to 27.5%–27.9%, versus 24.5%–24.9% as reported. Standalone fiscal 2027 free cash flow is guided to $3.4 billion–$3.9 billion; that guide excludes Filtration Group and CIRCOR.

The view moves toward the bear case if FY27–FY28 sell-through fails to confirm distributor orders, or if equipment use weakens. Aerospace schedule or supplier delays through FY29 would also reduce growth and cash conversion.

paragraphs.text: Parker has delivered against stated operating goals. Its February 2024 presentation set an adjusted earnings-per-share ambition of approximately US$30 for fiscal 2027, while fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings reached US$32.31. Adjusted figures remove selected costs, so they are useful only when the target and later result use the same definition. Parker also reached its fiscal 2029 adjusted segment operating-margin target three years early.

blocks.heading: What do Parker's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Sales reached $5,755 million, up 9.8% from the prior-year quarter. Organic growth was 8.0%, which means the improvement remained visible after removing ownership and currency effects.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Parker's next results?

paragraphs.text: The first checkpoint is the September quarter. Filtration Group was expected to be neutral to adjusted EPS at first, so its sales should not automatically be treated as an earnings gain. Investors should separate acquired revenue, underlying growth, financing expense and integration costs. The purchase-price allocation will also determine future amortization charges.
